svg.title: The Quantus engine, every path
svg.text: How quantus-core turns an input into a result, the working and the errors: all commands, all node types, all modes except Electronics.
Read each panel top to bottom. A circled letter jumps to the panel with that letter. Taken from the code on the dev branch.
What a transport (the Tauri shell) calls in api.rs. Each one is a function without state of its own; the SessionStore holds sessions and settings.
Only through the API, the app
Sessions are keyed by the id
Settings: the store's, shared by all sessions.
Precision: the request's if it has one, else the setting.
Variables: the session's, as exact quantities, keyed like v_1 or \omega_0.
A LatexCalculator is built with precision and settings; the mode decides how the input is read (panel B, right).
Numbers keep their decimal form as text: 9{,}81, 9,81 and 9.81 all become 9.81; no float ever.
Tokens: numbers, identifiers (letter runs, Greek commands), commands, operators, |, &, \\, braces.
An empty input or a character it does not know: error with its position.
A line that is not an equation:
An identifier, optionally with a subscript, directly followed by =: F =, v_1 =.
Note: x = 2x + 1 is read the same way. x becomes a label and 2x + 1 an
expression, so it is simplified, not solved.
Atoms: numbers, identifiers (see the right), \frac, \sqrt[n]{}, functions (\sin
^\circ, factorial, floor, ceil, mod, max, min, and \mathrm, \text, \qty (where
every identifier must be a unit).
Anything else: error naming the position.
a third = → Only one '=' is allowed
Every / becomes \frac{}{} with ordinary precedence: a \cdot b / c = \frac{a \cdot b}{c}; a chain shares one denominator,
a/b/c = \frac{a}{b \cdot c}; brackets end a chain.
→ that variable. Wins over units and constants, so i in \sum_{i=1}^{3} i is the index.
→ a variable: v_1, \omega_0. Only these can be defined.
2 The longest run of identifiers is a unit?
→ a unit: kg, mN, \mu m (µm). Greedy, so m s is a millisecond; products of units need \cdot.
Skipped in Algebra, Imaginary and Analysis mode.
a and y are variables unless 'a and y as variables' is off.
t, u and in are units only with 'extra unit letters'.
→ \pi, e; i is the imaginary unit only in Imaginary mode, otherwise a variable.
4 A single letter or Greek letter?
→ a free variable without index: x, \theta.
5 A run of letters that are each a variable?
Only with 'letter products'; xm stays an error.
6 otherwise: parse error naming the position
evaluate: from the LaTeX string to a tree. The same parser serves Analysis mode (panel G).
Letters without subscript and without a value, outside whatever binds
them; sorted alphabetically: x, y, z.
None: 'The system has no unknown to solve for.'
Read off one row per equation
Residual r = left − right, evaluated exactly with the unknowns put in.
constant: r(0, …, 0); coefficient a_j: r(e_j) − r(0)
check at three more points built from 2, −7/3, 5, 11/2, −1000
The check misses, or r is undefined at a point: The system is not
A dimension mismatch or a variable without value: that error.
Column by column: swap rows to get a pivot, divide the row by its pivot,
subtract multiples from the other rows. Every operation is logged with
infinitely many: each pivot unknown in terms of the free ones, x = 1 -
y ∧ y ∈ ℝ (ℂ in Imaginary mode)
Each value is presented as in panel D.
SUBSTITUTED: when it uses session variables
Standard only: the reduced matrix, 'Eliminate column by column'
A letter without subscript and without a value, outside whatever binds it.
None: 'The equation has no unknown to solve for.' Several: 'more than one unknown (x, y)'.
x is put into a copy of the session variables; both sides are evaluated exactly (panel E) and
subtracted. The unknown is a plain number, so both sides need one dimension.
A dimension mismatch or a variable without value: that error, at once.
Any other failure at a point (ln of a negative number): no value there.
Fit a quadratic through f(0), f(1), f(2)
one of the three undefined: not a quadratic, go numeric
Does f equal ax² + bx + c at
D > 0: two roots, sorted by value
the one below the axis first
D < 0 otherwise: This equation has no real

just beside the point (± step/1024), so a

root if |f| does not shrink (a pole like

only the 6 smallest minima are refined
The 6 roots nearest 0, sorted, rounded to
None: No solution for x found between −100
Each root is simplified and presented (panel D); the first one is the calculation's quantity.
SYMBOLIC, SUBSTITUTED (with session variables), RESULT. No lines in between: the solver writes
is not a session variable, not a
and not bound by Σ, ∫, lim or
π, e, roots and i; units
To a named unit: kg·m/s² → N. A
LatexCalculator::evaluate. A system, an equation, or anything else.
from a system, an equation or an evaluated expression
The decimal to the precision p.
'Exact roots': a value built from rationals and rational powers of rationals is written exactly: 2√3, π/2, √2/2. Anything else (e,
functions) falls back to the decimal.
Not a real number, Imaginary mode: a + bi, both parts to the precision (exactly with 'exact roots').
Not a real number otherwise: '2·i is not a real number and cannot be shown as a decimal.'
The unit is formatted, the quantity named (force, energy, …) when it has a name.
Is the input just its result (a definition m₁ = 2kg)? Then only RESULT.
SUBSTITUTED: when the input uses variables and putting their values in changes the line. A display line only: the decimals at
precision p; the arithmetic ran on the exact values.
Standard, not for equations: 'Convert to a common unit' when a sum has quantities in different units (5 km + 0,3 km).
Maximal: the order of operations, one kind at a time: 3 · 9² - 6/4 → 3 · 81 - 6/4 → 243 - 1,5.
Standard: 'Multiply the numbers and the units' when the raw unit is not the named one: 24 (kg · m²)/s² before 24 J.
Systems (C), equations (C) and algebraic results (F) bring their own lines and levels.
None: the list is hidden, the engine still works at Brief.
Brief: one line per rule. Standard (default): what a student writes. Detailed: every intermediate expression. Maximal: also
signs, order of terms, domain notes.
Every step carries the lowest level that shows it, and optionally the level from which a longer line replaces it.
key, symbol, LaTeX, value, unit and exact
quantity. A later definition replaces it.
latex: the finished line F = 20 N; result: without the label
steps: kind (symbolic, substituted, algebraic, note, result), LaTeX, rule, explanation, before and after
alignBlock: the whole calculation as one align* block for copying
value and imaginary: full precision, unformatted
variable: when the input defined one
warning: when the result is shown as typed because its variables have no value
Every red exit in panels B to F ends here: a message in the setting's language, and the position for parse errors only. Nothing is
The kinds of QuantusError: Parse (with position), DimensionMismatch, UnresolvedVariable, NotReal, Other.
The common end of every evaluate call.
Its decimal text becomes an exact rational: 0,1 is 1/10.
1 times the unit; prefixes and compound units come from the
π and e stay symbolic; i is the imaginary unit (Imaginary
1. a session variable 2. a physical constant (c₀, h_P, ħ, k_B,
N_A, Rₘ, e₀, ε₀, μ₀, mₑ, …), Physics mode only 3. else
'v_9 has no value yet. Define it first.'
As they are; the fraction divides exactly.
Both sides need one dimension; the right side is converted to
Numbers and units multiply; 2kg · 5 m/s = 10 kg·m/s.
Exact where it can be: rational powers of rationals stay
Not real (√−4): NotReal, except in Imaginary mode.
n must be a positive whole number; then like a power 1/n.
A degree with a unit, or not whole.
The magnitude; in Imaginary mode the modulus of a + bi. The
Exact; n and k non-negative whole numbers.
sin … arctan, ln, log, lg, exp, sinh, cosh, tanh, cot, sec,
csc: the argument must be a plain number; the complex version
Re, Im, arg, overline: Imaginary mode only.
Whole-number bounds; the body term by term with the index
Bounds in one unit (a bare 0 takes the other one's). Kinks of
|…| are found on a 64-point grid, bisected, and split the
interval. Each piece: tanh-sinh quadrature at min(p, 30) digits
+ 8 guard digits, +10 per nested construct. Unit: integrand ×
Mapped to a finite interval: x = a + t/(1−t), x = b − t/(1−t),
or x = t/(1−t²), with the Jacobian. A sample beyond 10²⁰ that
The body at target ± 10^−(p+5) and ± 10^−(p+4) (one side for x
→ a⁺), or at ±10^(p+5) for ±∞. The samples must agree to
10^−(p−5), relative; the mean is rounded to the agreed digits.
They disagree or grow: 'The limit does not exist'.
power and function rules), then evaluated at |ₓ₌ₐ, or with the
No point: 'needs a point to be evaluated at'.
Solved (panel C); its first solution is the value.
A system must be the whole input.
A matrix is not a number: take its determinant.
Square, at most 8×8, entries of one dimension; exact cofactor
expansion; the unit to the power n.
n! up to 10 000, exact; floor, ceil and mod keep the unit; max
and min need one dimension and answer in the first one's unit.

Evaluation is recursive: each node evaluates its children first, so a sum inside an integral inside a limit works, each with its own bound variable. Errors travel up unchanged. The result is a PhysicalQuantity: an exact Value (rational, π, e, roots, i and their combinations)
with a unit. Decimals are made only when presenting (panel D).
Evaluator::evaluate in eval/evaluator.rs, numeric.rs, eval/derivative.rs. Each card is one kind of node.
Binomial form: Auto, Expanded, Binomial. ⚙ Complete the square: on/off.
Conditional identities: with condition (default) or only where they hold.
Step detail and cancel marks (struck through or coloured).
a root, a function, π, e or i, |…|, a non-integer power
Each distinct atom becomes a variable of its own (# for constants, ordered before the letters; ◆ for the rest, after them), so
the polynomial machinery can work around it: sin x + sin x = 2 sin x.
Sums, integrals, limits, derivatives, matrices and equations are opaque: kept whole and untouched.
An identity can remove a denominator before the pipeline sees it (logₐ(a²) = 2), so they are recorded first.
2. Every identity rule once, in this order algebra/identities.rs
exp and log values: ln 1 = 0, ln e = 1, e^(ln a) = a, exp(x) = eˣ
powers: rational exponent → root, (aˣ)ʸ = aˣʸ, aˣ aʸ = aˣ⁺ʸ, aˣ/aʸ, aˣ bˣ = (ab)ˣ
roots: nest, extract (√8 = 2√2, √a² = |a|), multiply (√u√u = u), merge (√a√b = √ab), rationalize denominators (also
with the conjugate); repeated so each sees the others' results
logs: ln a + ln b = ln(ab), ln a - ln b = ln a/b, values again
trig: symmetry sin(-x) = -sin x, tan as a quotient, Pythagoras, 1 + tan² x, double angles, quotient back to tan
absolute values: |-a| = |a|, |a²| = a², products and quotients into one |…|
Each rule names the conditions it needs (a ≥ 0, b ≥ 0 for √a√b = √ab). A condition already known to hold costs nothing;
With condition: rewrite, and the condition joins the domain: '…, for a ≥ 0'.
Only where they hold: no rewrite.
In round 2 and later: no rule changed anything → leave the loop.
4. The rational pipeline on the atomized tree (right)
Its steps and restrictions are collected, its result is the next round's start.
In the result, every step and every restriction. A step that only changed how an atom was written is dropped.
Restrictions are simplified against the atoms.
Sums, integrals and the like left inside: note 'cannot be fully simplified algebraically; supported rational
Stage 3: domain restrictions from the untouched input: denominators, nested reciprocal denominators.
A denominator that is 0 for every x.
Stage 2: normalize notation one kind at a time, each a step: division → fraction, negative exponent → fraction, double negation.
Auto: keep it expanded when the input was written in compact binomials ((x+3)², (a-b)(a+b), (x+4)² - 5), else write the result in
Expanded / Binomial: always that way. ⚙ Complete the square allowed or not.
The phases run in this strict order. Within a pass the pipeline only moves forward, so an expansion is never followed by a factoring
5 products, quotients and powers of fractions; signs
7 FIND_COMMON_DENOMINATOR: extend each fraction by what it misses of the LCD
12 CANCEL_COMMON_FACTORS; the zeros of a cancelled factor stay in the domain
13 NORMALIZE_EXPRESSION: expanded numerator; ⚙ denominator factored when it is a
product of several factors (Auto), or always expanded / factored
4. A state seen before: the steps
then factor back). Roll back to
it and abandon them. A second
After the pass: stopped, in rational normal form,
4 passes and still changing: stop, PassLimit.
Verify: the input and the result are compared at 5 rational test points for all variables; points that break the domain are skipped.
A mismatch: the input comes back unchanged, with a diagnostic. Nothing wrong is ever shown.
A stop reason becomes a note: 'the result is equivalent but may not be fully simplified'.
The domain restrictions collected along the way: x ≠ -2, 2.
with atoms: back to the round
A note on the input's domain is put first. Steps are filtered by the step detail: rewrites hidden at this level are merged into
the next shown line, and a rule whose own lines are hidden shows its summary instead. ⚙ Cancelled factors struck through or
No step, no restriction, and not a binomial kept on purpose: the input is shown as typed, with the warning 'The variable x has
no value, so the expression is shown as typed'.
Working: SYMBOLIC, one ALGEBRAIC line per shown step (a NOTE for notes), RESULT if the last line is not already the result.
Value 0 and no unit: the result is LaTeX, not a number.
algebra/: identities on atoms around a deterministic rational pipeline, every rewrite a recorded step.
The language of every text the engine writes: the setting's.
A budget of 3 s: a deadline the numeric loops deep inside check, so a hard function still answers in time.
Digits: the request's precision, else min(precision setting, 6).
A leading f(x) = (also with \left( \right), as MathLive writes it) or y = is blanked out with spaces, so error positions stay
Parsed by the calculator's parser (panel B) as in Algebra mode: no units, i is a variable.
An equation or a system: 'Enter a function, not an equation.'
A parse error: with its position.
asked for and named differently: error 'The function is written in t, but x was asked for.'
else the asked one, else the named one
else the free letters: none → x; one → that one
several: 'f may depend on one variable only … function families are not supported yet.'
One spelling for each thing: a quotient is a product with a negative power, a root a rational power, eᵘ and exp u are both exp,
the variable is just x. Simplifier, derivatives and integrals match on this tree.
A construct the tree has no form for: error.
Read off the tree as typed, before anything cancels:
denominators ≠ 0, ln of a positive argument, even roots of non-negative radicands (positive in a denominator), a variable
exponent's base > 0, arcsin and arccos between −1 and 1, tan away from its poles
u ≠ 0 is solved with solve_zero (panel H); u > 0 by cutting the domain of u at its zeros and testing the sign in each piece;
zeros found numerically are said so
holes recorded; the working is the domain section
The period of f from its periodic parts sets the window to one period each side (±π for sin x); without one the window is [−10,
10]. f = ax + (periodic) is noted, the points then move with their family.
Each from the simplified one before it, with the working of the outermost rule: sum and factor rule, power rule, product rule
(u, v, u′, v′), quotient rule (or power and chain rule when the numerator is constant), chain rule with the inner function, the
Simplifying (analysis/simplify.rs): bottom-up until nothing changes; flat sums and products, folded constants, like terms,
exp/ln and radical rules, exact trig values; a rational part goes through the algebra pipeline (panel F).
derivatives, domain, symmetry, y-intercept, zeros, extrema, inflection, monotonicity, curvature, behaviour, antiderivative
The section comes back partial with the note
Its working, its result line and its status: ok, partial
(found numerically in a window, or undecided) or failed. A
section that runs out of time while it works is marked
Sections refer to points by a token until all are known; then they are named by kind and order: Z₁ zeros (N in German), S_y,
Max/H, Min/T, I/W inflection, S saddle, G/L hole, boundary extrema.
The default window from the points; breaks at the gaps and poles of D; 600 samples (sampling, panel J).
function, variable; sections (id, title, status, message, steps filtered by the step detail, result); points; asymptotes; the
Errors leave as ErrorResponse, as in panel D.
f′(x) = …, f″(x) = …, f‴(x) = …, each with its working (left).
The conditions as steps, then D = … (left).
D not symmetric about 0 (excluded families included): 'No symmetry: D is not symmetric about 0'.
f(−x), simplified; ⚙ Standard: x replaced by −x, and f(x), −f(x) for comparison.
f(−x) − f(x) = 0 symbolically: symmetric about the y-axis; f(−x) + f(x) = 0: about the origin.
neither: both tested at 9 points of D; a match says '(checked numerically)'.
0 ∉ D: none. Else f(0), exact; ⚙ Standard: worked out with 0 put in. Point S_y.
f(x) = 0 by solve_zero (panel H). f ≡ 0: 'f is 0 everywhere'.
multiplicity ≥ 2 noted: a double root touches the axis, a triple one crosses it
periodic f: the general solution x = π/2 + kπ, the members in the window marked
Necessary: f′(x) = 0 (solve_zero), plus the points of D where f′ is undefined (kinks). f′ constant: 'f is constant' or 'No
f″ defined and ≠ 0 there: f″ < 0 maximum, > 0 minimum ('Sufficient condition'); ⚙ Standard: the value put in
otherwise the sign of f′ just left and right, between the neighbouring candidates, gaps and ends: + to − maximum, − to +
Closed ends of D: boundary maximum or minimum by the sign of f′ just inside. y-values worked out (⚙ Standard).
f″(x) = 0 plus the points where f″ is undefined. f″ constant: 'f is linear' or none.
f‴ ≠ 0 there: an inflection point; otherwise the sign change of f″ decides
f′ = 0 there as well: a saddle point
periodic: families of one kind with the same y half a period apart are one family, W(kπ | 0) for sin x
The sign of f′ on each interval between its zeros and gaps in D, tested at the simplest point of the interval (a sign table):
strictly increasing on …, strictly decreasing on …; periodic f: one period, 'continued periodically'. f′ constant: 'f is
The same with f″: left-curved (convex) on …, right-curved (concave) on …; linear f: no curvature.
10 Behaviour at the edges and asymptotes
Panel I. None found: partial, 'No elementary antiderivative found'.
analyze in analysis/. Stateless: everything comes with the request; the session is not touched.
from zeros, extrema, inflection points, the domain and the area
e is f, f′, f″ or a domain condition; with it come D, the window and the digits.
Every step below is a line of the working.
0: every x, 'f is 0 everywhere'. Otherwise 'No solution' (c ≠ 0). On
A sum that simplifies to a product is factored first: step 'Factor out'.
a constant factor other than ±1: 'A constant factor is never zero'
factors below the line: only the numerator matters, 'a fraction is zero where its numerator
one factor left: solve_factor; several: the zero-product rule u = 0 ∨ v = 0, each through
never zero (eᵘ, u² + 1, a positive constant): 'This factor is never zero'
uʳ with r > 0: solve u, multiplicity times r
A power is solved like a factor first; anything else comes here.
'Factor out xᵏ': xᵏ · (…) = 0, then xᵏ = 0 ∨ (…) = 0; the rest from the top of
The pq formula (German, or when set) or the abc formula; the discriminant
decides: two roots, a double one, or none.
'Isolate the power': the n-th root, ± for even n; none when an even root meets a
Substitution z = xᵐ: a quadratic in z, then back to x.
Candidates ±p/q listed when both end coefficients are at most 1000; a root is
guessed and checked, then divided off by long division with its working
(analysis/polydiv.rs); the quotient from the top of this list.
Numerically inside the Cauchy bound, and said so; the section becomes partial.
Exactly one term depends on x: coefficient · outer + constants.
outer is x itself: 'Solve for x'
outer is a function, or a power with a constant base or exponent: 'Isolate the function', sin(2x) = 1/2, then invert it:
eᵘ = c → u = ln c for c > 0, else none
the root or the power, ± for even exponents; aᵘ = c → a logarithm
the principal values (exact at multiples of π/6 and π/4) plus 2kπ, or kπ for tan: a periodic family
sin, cos or tan of the value, if it lies in the range
u = each value, from the top of solve_zero; families stay families.
Not invertible, or more than one term depends on x: D ∩ [−100, 100] is scanned, 4000 samples over the whole range (at least 200 per piece), sign changes and touches refined; at most
A root outside D: 'Not in the domain, so no solution', x = 0 ∉ D.
Equal roots found twice are merged, their multiplicities added; families merged; members of a family that D leaves out are named.
Back to the caller with roots, families, the working and whether it is complete.
solve_zero: f(x) = 0 the way a student solves it
analysis/solve.rs. Exact where a school method applies, numerically, and said so, where none does. The first strategy that fits takes the equation.
The outer ends of D (−∞, +∞ or an open end), the gaps between its pieces, and the families D excludes (the poles of tan).
Every approach becomes t → ∞: x = t, x = −t or x = a ± 1/t.
rational functions: the degrees decide (at ±∞), or the sign next to the pole
otherwise growth orders: a term behaves like c · eᵇᵗ · tᵃ · (ln t)ˡ, the largest (b, a, l) wins
whatever that does not decide is sampled numerically; still unknown → the section is partial
a finite limit L: horizontal asymptote y = L, one line when both sides agree, else 'for x → ∞'
±∞ with a linear part: oblique asymptote y = mx + b, by polynomial division for rational f, else by limits; found numerically it
a rational f whose numerator degree exceeds the denominator's by 2 or more: the approximating curve, the polynomial part
the one-sided limits grow: vertical asymptote x = a, the limits shown
they meet at a finite value: a removable gap, marked as point G (L)
an excluded family: vertical asymptotes x = π/2 + kπ, the members in the window drawn
With the sum and factor rule; inner functions may be linear: ∫ cos(2x+1) dx = 1/2 sin(2x+1).
u = g(x) when the integrand is h(g(x)) · g′(x).
xⁿ eᵃˣ, xⁿ sin(ax), xⁿ ln x, arctan x, eᵃˣ sin(bx).
f. Only a match is shown: no

x₀ ∉ D, f(x₀) not exact, or f′ undefined there: 'f is not

m = 0: the tangent is horizontal, so the normal is vertical,

The tasks beside the curve sketch
analysis/tasks.rs and analysis/plot.rs. Stateless, each with its own budget.
